lessons: A browser-level check (preinstalled Chromium + a scratch Playwright venv outside the project) catches what string tests cannot: the reduced-motion specificity bug and the CSP data: requirement.
When a security fix replaces a framework default, compare against what the default protected: my first client_key widened trust beyond uvicorn's forwarded_allow_ips and the review caught it.
pkill -f <script> kills the shell running a restart command whose own command line names the script; kill by port (fuser -k 8765/tcp) instead.
Hash-pin vendored assets from the same publisher the SRI came from; the GitHub release build differs byte-wise from the npm build.
Mark a vendored directory -text in .gitattributes when a test pins its bytes; CRLF-published files would otherwise change on Windows checkout.
A mock cannot honestly refuse a field nobody has seen the server reject; the substitute is a rejection-path test plus the probe carrying the identical document.
A test asserting 'Camera' in a page that has a Camera tab asserts nothing; assert the section id.

dont_retry: Do not put the rest position, or any unmeasured field, into pet_status: a rejected field fails the whole document and takes battery, signal and the escape flag with it.
Do not add a CSP nonce; scripts are static files by design and the JSON data block needs none.
Do not fetch Leaflet from unpkg, jsdelivr or cdnjs in the sandbox (403); registry.npmjs.org works and only its build matches the pinned SRI.
Do not pkill -f a script from a command whose own line names it.
Do not believe a forwarded-address header from a non-loopback peer; keep KONA_TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS loopback-only unless the tunnel host really moves.
Do not add user-scalable=no, hard-code secure=True, or use location.reload() for refresh.
